flags.reason: Maternity needed within 12 months. Balanced's 12-month wait does not clear inside the horizon; the only plan that does (Comprehensive, 3-month wait) sits a band above the stated moderate budget.

recommendation.brokerReasoning: Maternity within a 12-month horizon is the binding constraint. Balanced covers maternity but behind a 12-month wait, which does not clear inside the horizon — covered on paper, unusable in practice. Comprehensive's 3-month wait clears with room, and its 25,000 maternity limit against a typical private delivery of ~40,000 leaves a known member share rather than a surprise. Placement is a deliberate one-band budget stretch (16,500 against a moderate ceiling of 10,000); the applicant accepted the trade. Flagged for reviewer because the stretch is the decision, not the arithmetic.
recommendation.memberReasoning: Comprehensive is the only plan on our panel where maternity cover actually starts in time for you. Balanced covers maternity too, but not until you have held the policy for 12 months — that is outside the window you told us about. Comprehensive starts covering it after 3 months. It costs more, at 16,500 a year, and maternity is capped at 25,000, so a private delivery will likely leave part of the bill with you.

rejections.reason: Maternity not covered at all. Excluded on benefit, not on price.
Maternity is covered but behind a 12-month waiting period, which does not clear inside the applicant's 12-month horizon. Cheaper, and unusable for the one thing they came for.
